claim: The C. elegans distal tip cell (DTC) is a canonical germ stem cell niche.
source: We discovered a mechanism of stem cell niche exit in the canonical C. elegans distal tip cell (DTC) germ stem cell niche mediated by previously unobserved, thin, membranous protrusions of the adjacent somatic gonad cell pair (Sh1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Thin, membranous protrusions of the adjacent somatic gonad cell pair (Sh1) mediate stem cell niche exit.
source: We discovered a mechanism of stem cell niche exit in the canonical C. elegans distal tip cell (DTC) germ stem cell niche mediated by previously unobserved, thin, membranous protrusions of the adjacent somatic gonad cell pair (Sh1).
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by imaging data throughout the manuscript.

claim: A disproportionate number of germ cell divisions were observed at the DTC-Sh1 interface.
source: A disproportionate number of germ cell divisions were observed at the DTC-Sh1 interface.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claim: Stem-like and differentiating cell fates segregated across the DTC-Sh1 boundary.
source: Stem-like and differentiating cell fates segregated across this boundary.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by marker expression data in Figure 5.

claim: Spindles polarized and pairs of daughter cells oriented between the DTC and Sh1.

evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by time-lapse imaging data in Figure 6.

claim: Sh1 grew over the Sh1-facing daughter cell.

evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by time-lapse imaging data in Figure 4.

claim: Impeding Sh1 growth by RNAi to cofilin and Arp2/3 perturbed the DTC-Sh1 interface.

source: Examples include stochastic displacement in the mammalian intestine (van der Flier and Clevers, 2009), migration in the larval tracheal system of Drosophila (Chen and Krasnow, 2014), oriented division to a basal lamina in the mammalian epidermis (Poulson and Lechler, 2010), and oriented division to the niche cells in the Drosophila ovary (Casanueva and Ferguson, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Migration is a mechanism of stem cell niche exit in the larval tracheal system of Drosophila.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The C. elegans germ line is supported by a canonical stem cell niche called the distal tip cell (DTC).
source: The C. elegans germ line is supported by a canonical stem cell niche (Hubbard, 2007; Lander et al., 2012) called the distal tip cell (DTC).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The first demonstration of stem cell niche properties was obtained from the C. elegans system.
source: Because of the ease of visualization and experimental manipulation, many general principles have been obtained by analysis of this simple system, including the first demonstration of stem cell niche properties (Kimble and White, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The genetics controlling stemness and differentiation in the C. elegans germ line are very well understood.
source: The genetics controlling stemness and differentiation are very well understood (Hubbard, 2007; Kimble and Seidel, 2013), and a cell biological understanding of the system is growing (Amini et al., 2014; Byrd et al., 2014; Linden et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The adult DTC has a jellyfish-like appearance, with a flattened cell body at the distal end and long trailing processes that extend proximally and enwrap germ cells.
source: The adult DTC has a jellyfish-like appearance, with a flattened cell body at the distal end and long trailing processes that extend proximally and enwrap germ cells, including the presumptive stem cells (Byrd et al., 2014; Crittenden et al., 2006; Gordon et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The C. elegans germ line is partially syncytial, with membrane-bound germ cell bodies connected to a common cytoplasmic core (the rachis) by narrow bridges of cytoplasm.
source: The germ line is partially syncytial, with membrane-bound germ cell bodies connected to a common cytoplasmic core (the rachis) by narrow bridges of cytoplasm (Hirsh et al., 1976; Seidel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The cytoplasmic connections in the C. elegans germ line facilitate the sharing of intracellular fate determinants.
source: Despite the cytoplasmic connections that facilitate the sharing of intracellular fate determinants (Lee et al., 2016), the germ line segregates cell fates across its distal-proximal axis, with germ cells undergoing meiosis proximal to the undifferentiated germ cells dividing stochastically in the distal 'progenitor zone'.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The progenitor zone is approximately 20 germ cell diameters long (~100 μm).
source: The progenitor zone is approximately 20 germ cell diameters long (~100 μm) and contains 243 + / - 25 cells in one-day adult animals (Crittenden et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The progenitor zone contains 243 +/- 25 cells in one-day adult animals.
source: The progenitor zone is approximately 20 germ cell diameters long (~100 μm) and contains 243 + / - 25 cells in one-day adult animals (Crittenden et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The DTC niche expresses the Notch ligands LAG-2 and APX-1 that activate Notch signaling in the germ stem cells.
source: The DTC niche expresses the Notch ligands LAG-2 and APX-1 that activate Notch signaling in the germ stem cells (Henderson et al., 1994; Nadarajan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: It has been hypothesized that divisions within the stem cell population simply push daughters out of the niche to eventually differentiate.
source: It has been hypothesized that divisions within the stem cell population simply push daughters out of the niche to eventually differentiate (Rosu and Cohen-Fix, 2017), however stem cell progeny breaking contact with the niche have not been visualized.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Stem cell progeny breaking contact with the niche have not been visualized.
source: It has been hypothesized that divisions within the stem cell population simply push daughters out of the niche to eventually differentiate (Rosu and Cohen-Fix, 2017), however stem cell progeny breaking contact with the niche have not been visualized.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this study.

claim: When the DTC is asymmetrically shaped, only the germ cells closest to it express a Notch reporter.
source: When the DTC is asymmetrically shaped, only the germ cells closest to it express a Notch reporter, and other equally distal germ cells lack reporter expression, suggesting that close proximity to the DTC rather than distal position defines stem cells (Linden et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Close proximity to the DTC rather than distal position defines stem cells.
source: When the DTC is asymmetrically shaped, only the germ cells closest to it express a Notch reporter, and other equally distal germ cells lack reporter expression, suggesting that close proximity to the DTC rather than distal position defines stem cells (Linden et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature and inference from the data.

claim: The remainder of the somatic gonad proximal to the DTC comprises five pairs of gonadal sheath cells that lie between the germ cells and the gonadal basement membrane.
source: Proximal to the DTC, the remainder of the somatic gonad comprises five pairs of gonadal sheath cells that lie between the germ cells and the gonadal basement membrane (Hall et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Sheath cell pair 1 (Sh1) covers germ cells in the distal gonad, with one cell on its superficial surface closer to the cuticle and the other on the deep surface closer to the gut.
source: Sheath cell pair 1 (Sh1) covers germ cells in the distal gonad, with one cell on its superficial surface closer to the cuticle and the other on the deep surface closer to the gut (Hall et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A ~20 germ cell diameter-long (~100 μm) 'germ line bare region' has been described between the distal boundary of Sh1 and the DTC.
source: Between the distal boundary of Sh1 and the DTC, a ~ 20 germ cell diameter-long (~100 μm) 'germ line bare region' has been described, in which germ cells are thought to contact the gonadal basement membrane directly, not somatic cells.
evidence: This is a statement about previous models in the field.

claim: In the germ line bare region, germ cells are thought to contact the gonadal basement membrane directly, not somatic cells.
source: Between the distal boundary of Sh1 and the DTC, a ~ 20 germ cell diameter-long (~100 μm) 'germ line bare region' has been described, in which germ cells are thought to contact the gonadal basement membrane directly, not somatic cells.
evidence: This is a statement about previous models in the field.

claim: Evidence for the bare region comes from scanning EM of dissected gonads and cytoplasmic GFP expressed in the gonadal sheath.
source: Evidence for the bare region comes from scanning EM of dissected gonads and cytoplasmic GFP expressed in the gonadal sheath (Hall et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing was used to endogenously tag cell membrane-localized gap junction proteins (INX-8 and INX-9).
source: To investigate how the elaborate DTC germ line stem cell niche interacts with other cells in the gonad we used CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing (Dickinson et al., 2015; Dickinson et al., 2013) to endogenously tag cell membrane-localized gap junction proteins (INX-8 and INX-9) that were previously found to be expressed in the DTC and the gonadal sheath cells (Starich et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study.

claim: INX-8 and INX-9 were previously found to be expressed in the DTC and the gonadal sheath cells.

claim: The N-terminus of C. elegans INX-6 is extracellular, flexible, and located in the pore of the gap junction.
source: The atomic structure of another C. elegans innexin, INX-6, has been determined (Oshima et al., 2016); the N-terminus of C. elegans INX-6 is extracellular, flexible, and located in the pore of the gap junction.

claim: The long cellular processes of the DTC niche cell were directly bordered by membranous extensions from Sh1.
source: Upon coexpression of each of these tagged innexins with a DTC membrane marker and examination by live-animal confocal microscopy, we observed expression in the DTC and in the gonadal sheath. Unexpectedly, we found that the long cellular processes of the DTC niche cell were directly bordered by membranous extensions from Sh1 (Figure 1A and B), contrary to the accepted model of gonad anatomy with a bare region separating DTC and Sh1 (Figure 1A, Lints and Hall, 2018).
evidence: This is a key finding of the study supported by imaging data in Figure 1.

claim: The finding that DTC processes are directly bordered by Sh1 extensions is contrary to the accepted model of gonad anatomy with a bare region separating DTC and Sh1.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that the long cellular processes of the DTC niche cell were directly bordered by membranous extensions from Sh1 (Figure 1A and B), contrary to the accepted model of gonad anatomy with a bare region separating DTC and Sh1 (Figure 1A, Lints and Hall, 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous models in the field.

claim: The Sh1 membrane protrusions can extend farther distal than the brightest cytoplasmic GFP signal in the cell.
source: We verified this pattern with another endogenously tagged protein that localizes to the membrane, integrin α subunit INA-1::mNeonGreen (Jayadev et al., 2019; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) and by crossing our mKate::INX-8 strain to a strain expressing cytoplasmic GFP (tnIs6(lim-7p::GFP) [Hall et al., 1999]) to reveal that the Sh1 membrane protrusions can extend farther distal than the brightest cytoplasmic GFP signal in the cell (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The extensive DTC-Sh1 interface is variable among individuals.
source: Unlike other cells in C. elegans, including even elaborately branching neurons (Chisholm et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2010; Zou et al., 2015), the extensive DTC-Sh1 interface is variable among individuals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) and uneven around the circumference of the gonad (Figure 1D shows superficial and deep Sh1 cells above and below the germ line, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and 1E.

claim: The DTC-Sh1 interface is uneven around the circumference of the gonad.
source: Unlike other cells in C. elegans, including even elaborately branching neurons (Chisholm et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2010; Zou et al., 2015), the extensive DTC-Sh1 interface is variable among individuals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) and uneven around the circumference of the gonad (Figure 1D shows superficial and deep Sh1 cells above and below the germ line, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 1D.

claim: The larval Sh1 cells were thin, elongated, irregular cells that extended away from the midline over the germ cells and reached towards the DTC with at least one long, thin projection.
source: To visualize the Sh1 cell during gonad formation, we examined mKate2::INX-8, which was expressed in the DTC and Sh1 cell membranes during gonadogenesis, along with a DTC membrane marker (Figure 2B). We found that the larval Sh1 cells were thin, elongated, irregular cells that extended away from the midline over the germ cells and reached towards the DTC with at least one long, thin projection (Figure 2B, arrows); the DTC sent at least one reciprocal projection back to touch Sh1 (n = 27/28 gonad arms have DTC and Sh1 in apparent contact).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 2B.

claim: The DTC sent at least one reciprocal projection back to touch Sh1 during larval development.
source: We found that the larval Sh1 cells were thin, elongated, irregular cells that extended away from the midline over the germ cells and reached towards the DTC with at least one long, thin projection (Figure 2B, arrows); the DTC sent at least one reciprocal projection back to touch Sh1 (n = 27/28 gonad arms have DTC and Sh1 in apparent contact).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 2B.

claim: In 27/28 gonad arms, DTC and Sh1 were in apparent contact during larval development.
source: We found that the larval Sh1 cells were thin, elongated, irregular cells that extended away from the midline over the germ cells and reached towards the DTC with at least one long, thin projection (Figure 2B, arrows); the DTC sent at least one reciprocal projection back to touch Sh1 (n = 27/28 gonad arms have DTC and Sh1 in apparent contact).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study.

claim: Thin projections between DTC and Sh1 persisted as the forming gonad made its first turn (n = 16/17).
source: These thin projections persisted as the forming gonad made its first (n = 16/17) and second (n = 10/10) turns (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study supported by imaging in Figure 2B.

claim: Thin projections between DTC and Sh1 persisted as the forming gonad made its second turn (n = 10/10).
source: These thin projections persisted as the forming gonad made its first (n = 16/17) and second (n = 10/10) turns (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study supported by imaging in Figure 2B.

claim: By the end of L4, the Sh1 came to rest with a smooth distal boundary approximately one germ cell diameter from the DTC.
source: By the end of L4, the Sh1 came to rest with a smooth distal boundary approximately one germ cell diameter from the DTC, which typically extended one or more short, thin projections that touched or nearly touched the distal Sh1 boundary (n = 14/17 within one germ cell diameter at the end of migration).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study.

claim: At the end of L4, the DTC typically extended one or more short, thin projections that touched or nearly touched the distal Sh1 boundary (n = 14/17 within one germ cell diameter at the end of migration).
source: By the end of L4, the Sh1 came to rest with a smooth distal boundary approximately one germ cell diameter from the DTC, which typically extended one or more short, thin projections that touched or nearly touched the distal Sh1 boundary (n = 14/17 within one germ cell diameter at the end of migration).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study.

claim: The DTC and Sh1 share an intimate association during gonad migration in the larva.
source: We conclude that the DTC and Sh1 share an intimate association during gonad migration in the larva (schematic Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the imaging data presented.

claim: The sharp distal boundary between the DTC and Sh1 was dramatically remodeled beginning at the L4/adult transition, coincident with the elaboration of the DTC (n = 4/4).
source: The sharp distal boundary between the DTC and Sh1 was dramatically remodeled beginning at the L4/adult transition, coincident with the elaboration of the DTC (n = 4/4, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study supported by imaging in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: As the DTC elaborated, Sh1 filled in the gaps between extending DTC processes (n = 13/14 young adults).
source: As the DTC elaborated, Sh1 filled in the gaps between extending DTC processes (n = 13/14 young adults, Figure 2B and Figure 2D) instead of residing in the middle of the distal arm of the gonad as was previously thought (Hall et al., 1999; Killian and Hubbard, 2005; Korta and Hubbard, 2010).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study supported by imaging in Figure 2B and 2D.

claim: Sh1 does not reside in the middle of the distal arm of the gonad as was previously thought.
source: As the DTC elaborated, Sh1 filled in the gaps between extending DTC processes (n = 13/14 young adults, Figure 2B and Figure 2D) instead of residing in the middle of the distal arm of the gonad as was previously thought (Hall et al., 1999; Killian and Hubbard, 2005; Korta and Hubbard, 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous models in the field.

claim: It has been hypothesized that the distal boundary of Sh1 would need to treadmill over germ cells to counter the distal-to-proximal movement of the underlying germ cells.
source: It has been hypothesized that the distal boundary of Sh1 would need to treadmill over germ cells to counter the distal-to-proximal movement of the underlying germ cells from the distal stem cell zone towards the bend (Hall et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Time-lapse imaging of Sh1 and the DTC found support for the hypothesis that Sh1 treadmills over germ cells.
source: We found support for this hypothesis from time-lapse imaging of Sh1 and the DTC (Figure 2—video 1, Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data.

claim: Sh1 almost always (n = 12/13) appeared to rapidly remodel its edges, moving both towards and away from the DTC on a scale of minutes.
source: While the DTC was sometimes observed to stretch proximally, Sh1 almost always (n = 12/13) appeared to rapidly remodel its edges, moving both towards and away from the DTC on a scale of minutes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
